title: Someone built a Kalshi ↔ Polymarket arb bot on our API and it's been running nonstop
author: Interesting_Ear_2124
selftext:
Small win I wanted to share.  
  
I've been building Layer (uselayer.sh), an API that tells you when a market on Kalshi and a market on Polymarket are the same thing. Same game, same Bitcoin window, same outcome, lined up so you don't have to match them by hand.  
  
About 6 days ago someone signed up and started building an arbitrage bot on top of it. It watches Kalshi and Polymarket for the same market at different prices. Since then it's made over 20K calls to Layer, mostly on the 15-minute crypto windows, with sports too.  
  
Matching markets across venues is the boring part everyone has to build first, and it's easy to get wrong. Different names for the same team, different times, rules that look the same but pay out differently. Seeing someone skip all that and go straight to the fun part is exactly why I built this.  
  
If you're building a bot across Kalshi, Polymarket, Polymarket US, Novig or Hyperliquid, give it a try and tell me what's missing. Happy to help you get set up.

comments.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
comments.body:
I would suggest editing your body text and giving it a clickable link. It's a worthwhile thing, but you will lose users if people have to do some manual copy-pasting.   
Link: [uselayer.sh](http://uselayer.sh)

I will try this out for sure. 

But some basic questions here.

1) How do you get the data

2) Every exchange is working individually then how centrally you can arbitrage here? I mean they are the broker and they are the exchange I am not sure how arbitrage work in that scenario. Again I am not very well educated in this space so little explaination would be great.

3) Are these markets enough liquid that arbitrage works here?

4) Can you give a little technical walkthrough on how you came up with uselayer.sh?
